Design Philosophy And Layer Boundaries.summary: Keep scientific intent, executable facts, lifecycle control, numerical execution, and persisted evidence under separate authorities.

sections.heading: Public Boundary
items: Package roots expose application services and task/study contracts, not workflow steps, executors, provider adapters, or compatibility facades.

Web, CLI, local Python, remote RPC, and MCP call the same protocol-neutral application services. MCP lets Codex invoke the existing agent; it must not duplicate static/adaptive sequencing, scientific policy, recovery or result merging.
TaskSpec/TaskReport describe one calculation; StudySpec/StudyPlan/StudyReport describe relationships among complete tasks.

sections.heading: Authority
items: PlatformRegistry defines executable capabilities, modules, gates, providers, bindings, parameters, observables, and artifacts.
The LLM Wiki explains scientific policy and limitations but cannot enable execution; the UI owns presentation but cannot override validation.
State machines own lifecycle and approval; reports own structured outcomes; artifacts own large numerical evidence and provenance.

sections.heading: Composition
items: A module owns a reusable step, a capability belongs to a module, a provider supplies an implementation boundary, and a binding selects its runtime adapter.
Construct workflows top-down from requested capabilities and verify them bottom-up through module inputs, provider bindings, gates, and declared outputs.
Keep inseparable upstream self-consistent loops as composite provider modules instead of inventing unsupported intermediate APIs.

sections.heading: Scientific Control
items: The LLM may interpret requests and explain structured evidence; deterministic contracts, validation, gates, and providers control execution.
Initial study cases remain independent unless a dependency is declared; cross-case continuation and method promotion occur only in explicit analysis or refinement stages.
Use general diagnostics and registered evidence rather than benchmark-specific branches or molecule-specific thresholds.

The LLM owns free-text interpretation. Transport adapters must preserve its complete structured revision; they must not override scientific choices through keyword matching, inferred scan identities, or seed reconstruction.
Missing diagnostics are unavailable evidence, not a weak-correlation classification. Optional artifact failures retain valid numerical results but record the missing evidence and failure reason.
The backend owns executable review and recovery actions. Browser presentation must not invent actions absent from the workflow report.

sections.heading: Dependency Direction
items: The intended direction is public API to application services to contracts and registry to workflow runtime to providers and executors.
Extend the existing authority for a concern; do not add a second catalog, result format, workflow state, or compatibility facade.
Persist normalized inputs, generated PySCF scripts, logs, checkpoints, arrays, and plot data as registered evidence for reproducibility.

sections.heading: Scientific Input And Evidence Boundaries
items: The LLM returns explicit basis and coordinate proposals; request preparation does not authorize scientific defaults from keywords or summaries. Without an interpreter, an unapplied natural-language edit is unavailable, not ready.

Repeated adaptive normalization preserves request identity and sparse explicit provider choices. Shared owner contracts reject lossy integers, malformed options and invalid booleans; browser controls cannot replace filled invalid values with defaults.

Unknown classifications block routing. Missing UNO evidence is not zero fractionality. Nonphysical model occupations retain raw values and out_of_bounds status. Optional evidence generation records failure reasons while preserving completed energies.

Root assignment retains an exact best/runner-up ambiguity margin for every root count. Spin-free entropy fallback requires a verified SU(2) singlet; unavailable NPDM evidence on other spin sectors cannot justify that substitution.

Wiki Compilation Goals.summary: Keep the knowledge base as executable rules for CAFES.

sections.heading: Rule
items: Prefer canonical rule pages over repeated explanatory prose.
Each page must name the trigger, required action, forbidden action, validation gate, and failure pattern when applicable.
When a rule conflicts with a descriptive note, the rule wins.

sections.heading: Must
items: Use short imperative language: must, must not, reject, normalize, require approval.
Keep aliases in frontmatter rather than as visible folded-topic prose.
Use tables or bullet lists for contracts, fields, operation vocabularies, and approval matrices.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not keep duplicate rule bodies across pages.
Do not create dangling wiki links to pages that are not generated.
Do not expose raw chain-of-thought or hidden planner JSON as user-facing knowledge.

CAFES Architecture.summary: Defines the global system boundary between planning, execution, solver selection, state, artifacts, and approval gates.

sections.heading: System Layers
items: Planner layer decomposes user goals into approved cases.
Execution graph layer runs one normalized task specification at a time.
Molecular-correlation and model-Hamiltonian subpackages implement diagnostics and solver-specific behavior.
Solver layer maps validated molecular methods or model-Hamiltonian solvers to PySCF calls.
State/artifact layer keeps compact execution state separate from persisted files.
Approval layer separates conversation, plan construction, calculation execution, active-space review, and recovery review.
Application-service layer exposes the same task and study use cases to Web, CLI, local, and remote adapters.
Execution-target layer selects local or named Slurm infrastructure without changing the scientific task specification.
Web presentation uses small HTML shells, responsibility-scoped JavaScript/CSS package assets, and one shared molecular-preview implementation.
Task orchestration executes registered modules; study orchestration owns complete tasks, approvals, dependencies, cross-case analysis, refinement, and the merged report.
Molecular datasets reuse Study and Task: one trajectory per seed molecule, sampled AO matrices in artifacts, and separate dataset finalization, generation, and collection.

Web LocalProcessExecutor persists verified process identities and supports cancellation after restart. An independent POSIX supervisor enforces optional wall_time_seconds; the termination grace period is separate. Setting the local wall-time CLI flag also selects supervised execution for synchronous callers.
Optional immutable remote releases bind a local source fingerprint to the server runtime; deployment identity is execution infrastructure, not a scientific TaskSpec field.

sections.heading: Must
items: Execute only normalized task specifications.
Keep solver choice, charge, spin, reference, and method selection in the task-spec/execution layer.
Keep generated input files, logs, spectra, and structured results in run-directory artifacts.
Require approval gates before planner-generated execution.
Treat an MP2 active-space probe as a registered preparation role and preserve the requested CAS method, target solver, and solver options for the approved task.
Use one authoritative study lifecycle; derive presentation actions from it instead of maintaining competing workflow stages.
Rebuild the complete StudyReport from current saved Task/Run results in the backend; browser session state is only a view cache.
Keep server and resource-profile selection in execution metadata; servers own their queue, CPU, memory, and wall-time values.
Serve Assistant and Planner static assets from package resources and keep HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in package-data manifests.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not treat chat history as executable state.
Do not let UI defaults silently override the structured task specification.
Do not make a UI surface responsible for backend validation.
Do not infer study review type from special study ids, private plan keys, UI modes, or conversation text.

sections.heading: Current Migration Boundary
items: Study -> Task -> Run ownership and full-report merging across selected retries are implemented. New checkpoints store TaskReport references and compact status summaries; existing inline checkpoints remain readable.

Specialized scientific stages retain procedural adapters, and some review services transport a parent report and private stage fields. Typed review/stage adapters may improve these boundaries independently; a report-revision engine is not required for ordinary retries.
Task module handlers must return a dictionary, but completed traces record declared output names without validating every realized output port schema.

Public Data Contracts.summary: All application surfaces exchange the same versioned task, study, scheduler, and artifact structures.

sections.heading: MCP Adapter
items: The optional stdio MCP server exposes single-task validation, submission, status, collection and cancellation through CalculationApplicationService, using existing TaskSpec, JobHandle, JobStatus and TaskReport contracts.

Task monitoring uses CalculationApplicationService.inspect_task: the Web view and MCP show_task/app-only refresh_task_view read the same executor status, saved report summary and bounded log evidence. Automatic refresh makes no LLM calls, never collects or executes, and stops at terminal status. Solver metrics are last observed evidence, not final task energies or convergence decisions. open_task_monitor retains the exact JobHandle; SSH inspection requires the updated remote inspect-task RPC. Inline rendering depends on the host.

collect_task returns a named summary projection and full-report resource URI. Only the complete report carries the TaskReport schema; encoded handle references add no new task identity or persisted store.
Registry and packaged wiki resources retain separate authority. Scientific approval gates and convergence retries remain runtime-owned; MCP validation does not grant approval.

Study tools save static/adaptive preparation and start one background call to the existing agent runner. submit_study maps to application start_study; the per-task submit-only path is removed. Study ID survives client exit. Existing plans, checkpoints, reports and receipts remain authoritative. study-invocation.json and its inherited POSIX lock record only the latest application process, not another task state machine. Review decisions are saved in StudyReport.pending_review and require explicit start by Study ID; collection never submits work.

analyze_study calls deterministic agent diagnostics without an LLM or new calculations; existing MPS/path approvals start those services separately. prepare_dataset calls the existing dataset planner, Task validation and ordinary Study runner, exposing its accepted/rejected sample manifest. No protocol-owned scientific execution is added.

sections.heading: Stable Structures
items: TaskSpec is the validated request passed to one executor and TaskReport is its scientific result.
StudySpec defines a multi-case objective, StudyPlan expands executable cases, and StudyReport is the authoritative merged study record.
JobHandle and JobStatus describe scheduler identity and lifecycle without replacing scientific status.

Artifact references carry kind, path, size_bytes, mime_type, and description; registered JSON artifacts carry their own versioned schemas. Full initial_mo_coeff matrices use pyscf-agent.numeric-array.v1 NPY references with shape and dtype; only numerical consumers load arrays. Long presentation text stays in artifacts with bounded previews. JSON writes stream into atomic temporary files.
HamiltonianDatasetSpec, HamiltonianSample, rejection, and manifest contracts live in computational_study_agent.hamiltonian_dataset_contracts; StudyReport has a dataset_manifest field.
RuntimeIdentity describes the deployed source and public contract; large numerical arrays stay in registered artifacts.

sections.heading: Retry Persistence Compatibility
items: The existing study checkpoint gains execution_associations_version=1 and case execution associations containing run_id, receipt_path, pending, and the outer attempt number. Case dictionaries preserve these fields in StudyReport round trips.

Execution receipts record submission_unknown before handles are acknowledged. Explicit reconcile_execution verifies server-owned submission.json evidence against request fingerprints, case IDs, pending run IDs, and receipt ownership before restoring handles. Reconciliation never submits work; missing or partial evidence remains unknown.
Collect is an application-service operation without submission side effects. A subsequent conversion fix now also preserves top-level StudyReport extensions.

sections.heading: Contract Ownership
items: pyscf_agent.contracts owns TaskSpec, TaskReport, and task serialization helpers.
pyscf_agent.schema_contracts owns public schema identifiers, compatibility policy, and envelope validation; computational_study_agent.schema owns study dataclasses.
An LLM prompt, UI payload, scheduler record, or process-local PySCF object is never a public scientific contract.

sections.heading: Public API
items: pyscf_agent exposes CalculationApplicationService, TaskSpec, TaskReport, PlatformRegistry, and default_registry.
computational_study_agent exposes StudyApplicationService, StudySpec, StudyPlan, StudyCase, and StudyReport.
Executors and registry contracts remain in focused namespaces; workflow nodes, parsers, runners, retry helpers, provider adapters, and catalog builders remain internal.
Do not recreate the removed pyscf_agent_backend or backend.models compatibility facades.

sections.heading: Boundary Rules
items: Readers accept additive fields and must preserve them during read-write round trips.
Do not expose process-local PySCF objects; persist numerical arrays and pass registered artifact references.
Do not use a free-form dictionary as a second public TaskReport or StudyReport format.
Run and Collect return complete reports from current task checkpoints. Review subsets retain the original Study ID, and collection can load the saved plan by ID without a browser report.

sections.heading: Report Compatibility And Remaining Migration
items: StudyReport declares optional adaptive/postprocessing objects and preserves other accepted additive fields at their original top-level keys. Input, object, and exported nested values are independent copies.

The reader accepts base study-report.v1, existing adaptive-study-report.v1, and schema-less legacy base reports. Output preserves the input schema; schema-less input receives base v1. Missing optional extensions default to null, and empty objects remain empty.
Incompatible schemas and malformed known extensions are rejected; adaptive-schema input requires an adaptive object. Use to_dict() for serialization, not dataclasses.asdict().

The adaptive runner still returns its versioned dictionary. Preserving evidence fixes the former data-loss boundary; typed stage adapters and review context remain possible improvements. Ordinary retries merge current Task/Run outcomes without a report-revision engine.

sections.heading: Optional Evidence Status
items: Reference 1RDM capture failures appear in evidence_errors; CAS natural_occupation_evidence and t2_orbital_importance_evidence expose status and reasons. Successful numerical energies survive optional evidence-generation failures.

Model natural_occupation_summary preserves raw occupations and reports out_of_bounds beyond numerical roundoff, with null fractionality metrics. Consumers exclude unavailable/invalid evidence from scoring instead of interpreting it as weak correlation.

Study Orchestration And Report Authority.summary: Explains Study -> Task -> Run ownership, complete report updates, recoverable execution, and the remaining specialized-stage boundary.

sections.heading: Study, Task, And Run
items: A Study owns tasks (cases), and each task identifies its current run and attempt count. Approved review subsets retain Study and case IDs; retries create distinct run directories. Batch handles and receipts group submissions without a child Study.
The September 6 correction removes child registration, exported task-to-child references, and the separate integrate_review_execution API. Run and Collect return the complete StudyReport.

sections.heading: Persisted Responsibilities
items: study-plan.json retains the complete task set and latest task contracts. study-state.json owns current runs, receipts, attempt counts, task_report_ref pointers, compact task_summary status, and lifecycle. Collected TaskReports live in case-reports and are written before the checkpoint. Status reads do not load reports or arrays; collection explicitly reads report JSON. Legacy inline checkpoints remain readable without changing submitted input fingerprints. Optional review metadata records scientific stage kind and selected cases without execution ownership.

Receipts own scheduler batches or local case-to-JobHandle associations and transport status; TaskReports own scientific outcomes; StudyReport owns comparisons, analysis, and artifacts. Browser snapshots cannot replace current checkpoint results. No additional state framework or report revision system is required.

sections.heading: Execution And Recovery
items: Run executes an approved subset or explicit case/status selection while retaining unselected task results and contracts. It first recovers pending executions across the same Study rather than replaying a submission.

Background Start invokes existing run_study/run_adaptive_study once through completion, required review or interruption. The runner owns sequencing; MCP clients do not advance tasks manually. Invocation metadata and a POSIX lock identify the coordinator across client exits without replacing task state.

MCP Study tools call application services by saved Study ID. Direct-CAS preparation and probe review are shared with Web. Review saves its decision in StudyReport.pending_review for explicit start by Study ID; it never executes the decision itself.

Collect loads saved input and current handles without submitting failed or unstarted tasks. can_collect is false while the agent runs; scientific success is determined from StudyReport. An interrupted adaptive collection may prepare a stage which needs a later explicit Run.

Remote Collect and direct execution share complete-batch acceptance before checkpoint updates. Missing or extra cases and mismatched run identities cannot partially complete a batch. Unknown submissions require existing server evidence, not another submission.

sections.heading: Report Updates
items: Run/Collect rebuild the full comparison from current TaskReports, preserving unselected results, existing observables, unchanged annotations, and adaptive/postprocessing extensions. Scientific stage snapshots remain evidence within the same Study.

Final success requires successful current results for every task. Reports are atomically written after task results; same-process Run/Collect operations share the Study lock. Background start/review/collect share an inherited process lock across MCP servers; direct Python/Web Run should not overlap that writer.

sections.heading: Historical Data And Scope
items: Completed legacy child/stage records can be imported from saved checkpoints into the original Study checkpoint without submitting calculations or moving artifacts. Pending historical child execution must be collected before migration. Browser-only numerical reports cannot seed execution state.

Specialized initial/refined adaptive stages, MPS continuation, and bidirectional candidate evaluation retain their scientific orchestration and stage artifacts. This correction does not introduce a universal typed stage engine or a revision protocol.

Execution State Minimum Contract.summary: Execution state is a compact validated record for one task; planner and adaptive state add explicit campaign and review context.

sections.heading: Required Keys
items: `task_spec`: normalized canonical request for the selected system type.
`run_id` and `work_dir`: canonical execution identity and location.
`execution_status`, validation errors, attempts, messages, and logs.
generated input, structured/compact results, artifact references, and a versioned TaskReport after execution.
For adaptive studies: versioned workflow stage, plan kind, scope, allowed actions, and case-queue identifiers.

sections.heading: Forbidden Payloads
items: Do not store long PySCF stdout in state; store a log path plus compact preview.
Do not store full spectra in state; store artifact paths plus summary counts.
Do not store generated source code only in state; persist it as an artifact.
Do not store hidden chat/planner reasoning as execution truth.

sections.heading: Validation Checkpoints
items: Before execution, verify task type, method or solver, input path/spec, charge/spin/nelec, unit, and work directory.
Before planner run approval, verify every case against the task spec and capability registry.
After execution, verify artifact paths, structured result keys, energy units, and summary consistency.

sections.heading: Stale Triggers
items: Mark a plan stale when task input, work directory, method, solver, charge, spin, nelec, unit, operation list, or case table changes.
Require revalidation and renewed approval before executing stale planner output.
Regenerate previews from serialized state or artifacts, not from cached UI-only data.
After a subset recovery, rebuild adaptive state from the merged parent report.

Error Knowledge Base.summary: Failure pages convert observed bugs into permanent planner/executor rules.

sections.heading: Rule
items: Every recurring failure must map to a prevention rule and a regression test.
Error pages must include symptom, root cause, permanent rule, repair, and regression test.
Prefer short reproducible examples over narrative debugging history.

Three-Surface Separation Architecture.summary: Builder, single-calculation agent, and planner are separate UI/interaction surfaces with explicit handoffs.

sections.heading: Surfaces
items: Builder surface edits model-Hamiltonian geometry, parameters, boundary conditions, and saved input artifacts.
Single-calculation surface prepares and runs one molecular, periodic, or model-Hamiltonian task.
Planner surface turns a broader scientific request into approved cases that reuse single-calculation workflows.

sections.heading: Handoff Contract
items: Builder to agent/planner handoff is a saved input path plus target identifier.
Planner to single-calculation handoff is a normalized case task spec.
Single-calculation to planner handoff is structured results plus artifact paths.
Use target identifiers when the builder returns data to another surface.
Preserve each surface's state across navigation.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not couple builder UI state to solver execution state.
Do not infer solver choice from builder UI state.
Do not refresh the caller page when returning from builder navigation.
Do not reuse hidden UI state as scientific input.

Predefined Workflow Architecture.summary: The LLM proposes; the backend validates and executes through fixed workflow gates.

sections.heading: Rule
items: LLM may propose a task, edit a plan, or explain results.
Backend must normalize and validate before execution.
Tool selection is constrained by capability registries.
Prior context is not executable truth.
Expensive or risky steps require explicit user approval.

sections.heading: Validation
items: Reject unsupported methods, solvers, operations, or malformed electron counts.
Normalize scalar total electron requests into spin-resolved electron counts before execution.
Revalidate stale plans if input files, work directory, system type, or solver settings change.

sections.heading: Failure Example
items: A planner proposes `nelec: 3`; backend must convert or reject before running.
A user asks for Hartree-Fock but stale DFT defaults remain in UI state; backend must execute the normalized spec, not the stale default.

Capability Registry.summary: Planner freedom is bounded by registered runtime capabilities.

sections.heading: Rule
items: Every planner operation must correspond to a registered backend operation.
Every solver choice must correspond to a registered solver capability.
Unsupported actions are rejected or converted into a user-facing clarification.
Capability status must distinguish executable, design-only, planned, and reference-only features.

sections.heading: Must
items: Use the registry to validate operation names, argument shapes, supported methods, supported solvers, and postprocessing tools.
Derive study modes and adaptive initial-scan option ids from the Registry; serialize only canonical ids `auto`, `mp2`, and `fci`, with one method per full-grid initial plan.
Validate every emitted artifact kind and JSON payload schema against `artifact_contracts`, including the dynamic `observable-*` pattern.
Report validation failures before execution.
Keep human approval after plan building and before run submission.
Use audit tests to detect drift between registry facts, backend constants, planner operations, UI option ids, and generated capability exports.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not treat wiki text or PySCF reference coverage as execution support.
Do not put UI display labels, button text, layout, or helper copy into registry metadata.
Do not edit generated capability markdown by hand; regenerate it from the runtime registry.

LangGraph Workflow Graph.summary: LangGraph coordinates deterministic stages and state transitions.

sections.heading: Rule
items: Each graph node must consume and produce explicit state keys.
Graph edges represent allowed workflow transitions.
Human approval gates must appear before execution nodes for planner-generated campaigns.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not hide task-changing mutations inside display-only nodes.
Do not let an analysis node trigger a calculation unless the workflow edge explicitly allows it.

Workflow State Design Principles.summary: State is compact, structured, and separate from large artifacts.

sections.heading: Must
items: Store artifact paths instead of large stdout, spectra, or full generated code in workflow state.
Store compact summaries and structured result keys for LLM-visible context.
Version state schemas when adding new task families or result formats.
Persist `pyscf-agent.study-plan.v1`, `study-state.v1`, `study-report.v1`, and adaptive workflow/report schemas instead of relying on chat history.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not duplicate long stdout and parsed summaries in multiple state fields.
Do not rely on implicit defaults that are absent from serialized state.
Do not allow hidden state to diverge from the user-visible form.

sections.heading: Study Resume And Retry
items: Status and Collect never create an attempt. Run may retry within its existing approval and bounds; recovering persisted handles retains the current attempt.
Keep execution associations in the existing checkpoint rather than adding another retry workflow. Persist intent before submission and report unknown acknowledgement explicitly.
Invalid checkpoints and missing new-format associations are errors, not empty state. Adopt compatible legacy receipts conservatively without submitting jobs.

Planner Agent for Computational Campaign.summary: The planner builds multi-task campaigns from existing single-workflow capabilities.

sections.heading: Rule
items: Planner must decompose a campaign into cases that can each run through the existing single-calculation workflow.
Planner may generate sweeps, case designs, solver comparisons, and defect studies only through registered operations.
Planner must keep hidden planning state separate from user-facing summaries.

sections.heading: Must
items: Ask for or infer a base system before planning parameter changes.
Build a concrete case table before execution.
Require user approval for the case table and for running the campaign.

Planner Agent Approval Boundary.summary: Plan construction and plan execution are separate approval gates.

sections.heading: Rule
items: Build plan approval allows the planner to create a concrete case table.
Run approval allows the backend to execute approved cases.
Run Plan performs independent case calculations; cross-case continuity checks and AO 1RDM reuse begin only after the user selects Analyze Results.
Compatible block2 MPS reuse also begins only after Analyze Results and a fingerprinted continuation approval.
Any task-changing edit after approval invalidates the approved plan.
Active-space and recovery approvals apply to the selected case subset, not every failed case.

sections.heading: Must
items: Show the user the planned cases, changed parameters, solver/method, expected outputs, and work directory before run approval.
Detect stale plans when the model input file, work directory, method, solver, charge, spin, nelec, or operation list changes.
Require re-approval after stale-plan detection.
After a recovery subset completes, merge it into the parent report before showing further review or analysis.
Show a CAS candidate's deterministic resource estimate in the same ActiveSpaceAudit review; cost acknowledgement does not replace scientific active-space approval.
For MPS continuation, show target/source cases, checkpoint provenance, executor identity, parameter distance, orbital ordering, and quantum-sector compatibility before approval.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not start a calculation from a conversation send action.
Do not treat a planning draft as execution approval.
Do not hide case changes inside natural-language summaries.
Do not transfer an MPS across execution targets or incompatible orbital, electron, spin, symmetry, root, or ordering sectors.

Planner Workflow Validation.summary: Planner output must be checked, repaired, normalized, or rejected before it can enter execution.

sections.heading: Validate Plan Structure
items: Every plan must contain explicit cases or a deterministic rule for generating cases.
Every case must map to one single-calculation task specification.
Every operation must have a registered operation name and typed arguments.
Every case must declare the input artifact it mutates or reuses.

sections.heading: Registry Checks
items: Validate operation names against the capability registry.
Validate solver and method names against solver/method support.
Validate site indices, bond indices, electron counts, unit fields, and artifact paths.
Reject operations that require backend capabilities not yet implemented.
Static model scans preserve unchanged sites, bonds, nelec, boundary, and unit metadata from the base input.
Recovery subsets must preserve parent case identifiers and may mutate only the reviewed case.

For adaptive molecular studies, run the registered initial method over the full grid, preserve case identity, and select further methods only in reviewed refinement or recovery. Model studies retain an explicit solver and can opt into parameter-grid refinement; see [[Model Grid Convergence Barriers]].

sections.heading: Stale-Plan Checks
items: Invalidate a plan when the base input file, work directory, model parameters, method, solver, charge, spin, nelec, or operation list changes.
Require renewed plan approval after stale-plan detection.
Do not run a stale case table even if a previous run approval exists.

sections.heading: Repair / Normalize / Reject Policy
items: Normalize scalar total electron requests into spin-resolved `nelec` when the rule is unambiguous.
Repair harmless aliases such as method labels only when they map to one canonical backend value.
Reject ambiguous, unsupported, or lossy transformations and return a user-facing issue.

Accept the complete structured StudySpec returned by the Planner, including simultaneous global and case-local changes. Preserve explicit study mode and nested impurity-solver ownership; unsupported choices remain validation errors.

Expand explicit start/stop/step case-variable ranges in the shared StudySpec contract. Reject malformed or excessive ranges rather than truncating them or guessing which model parameter they represent.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not silently drop rejected operations.
Do not run a partially invalid plan unless the user explicitly approves the reduced plan.
Do not let LLM-generated scalar `nelec` reach execution.

sections.heading: Failure Example
items: `change_nelec` with a scalar value is invalid at execution boundary; normalize to `[nalpha, nbeta]` or reject with a repair instruction.

Adaptive Scan Workflow State Machine.summary: Adaptive scans use a versioned state machine so initial scan, approval, recovery, and full-report merge cannot be inferred only from chat history.

sections.heading: States
items: This method-routing state machine applies to adaptive molecular studies. Model studies retain an explicit solver under study_mode=static; optional grid_refinement changes sampling and has its own convergence barriers. Do not invent molecular initial-scan or active-space stages for model studies.

Use `pyscf-agent.adaptive-workflow.v1` with execution states such as `initial_plan_ready`, `cost_review_required`, `initial_scan_blocked`, `active_space_review_required`, `recovery_review_required`, `completed`, and `completed_with_issues`, plus analysis-triggered MPS-continuation, AO-1RDM-continuation, and path-refinement review states.
Keep full study plans distinct from refined and recovery subsets.
Cost review is tied to a deterministic plan estimate; active-space review remains a separate scientific approval even when both appear in one review surface.
Normal adaptive execution stores independent case results and a deferred path-analysis marker; it cannot enter continuation or path-refinement states before an explicit Analyze Results request.
For unresolved block2 cases, Analyze Results checks compatible same-executor MPS continuation first; approved retries run sequentially and merge into the parent report.

sections.heading: Review Modes
items: For unresolved or blocked cases, set `review_mode=case_queue` and expose only `current_case_id` actions.
For all ActiveSpaceAudit candidates in one executable refined, recovery, or path-refinement plan, set `review_mode=batch` and present their CAS evidence together.
Advance a failed-case queue only after rebuilding workflow state from the merged parent report.
Do not replay an approval request for a case that has already succeeded.
Offer case-specific actions such as CASSCF promotion, active-space expansion, bounded max-cycle increase, guarded FCI, or blocked-input guidance instead of a generic plan-table review.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not batch-approve non-equivalent failed cases.
Do not replace a full adaptive report with one recovery result.
Do not use conversation text as the recovery-state authority.

User-facing Planning Summaries.summary: The UI shows decisions and progress, not raw hidden reasoning.

sections.heading: Must
items: Show what the planner is checking, what plan it produced, what changed, and what needs approval.
Use concise progress messages for capability lookup, input inspection, validation, and plan drafting.
Present plans as tables or structured summaries.
Keep helper text concise and action-oriented in dense planner panels.
Keep each planner task session isolated with its own StudySpec, model input, work directory, run id, messages, plan, report, postprocessing specs, and artifacts.
Snapshot the current planner task before restoring another task.
Synchronize linked builder input paths into the seed StudySpec before LLM drafting.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not reveal private chain-of-thought.
Do not expose raw planner JSON as the primary UI.
Do not label approval as vague human approval; name the action being approved.

Model Hamiltonian Input Contract.summary: Model inputs are scientific artifacts that define structure, parameters, boundary conditions, and units.

sections.heading: Required Fields
items: model family such as Hubbard.
dimension, preset, boundary condition, sites, bonds, and electron count.
per-site onsite energy and Hubbard U when non-default.
per-bond hopping integral t and Coulomb repulsion V when non-default.
energy unit, written as `a.u.` when using atomic units.

sections.heading: Template Metadata
items: One-dimensional builder templates include chain, ring, zigzag chain, and quasi-1D ladder.
Two-dimensional builder templates include square, Lieb, honeycomb, triangular, kagome, dice, and square-octagon.
Template names are reproducibility metadata; execution must use exported sites, bonds, boundary condition, offsets, and parameters.
Periodic templates must preserve image offsets and allowed sublattice connectivity.

sections.heading: Must
items: Treat the saved model input file as the source of structure truth.
Store site and bond parameters explicitly when they differ from global defaults.
Preview periodic bonds using boundary markers rather than drawing misleading direct in-cell connections.
Keep solver choice outside the scientific model artifact.
Preserve valid wrap bonds in small periodic cells even when the displayed source-target pair is already directly bonded.
Display energy-like model parameters with the selected energy_unit wherever users inspect values.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not store solver choice in builder output.
Do not expose Holstein-Hubbard controls until an executable phonon solver and its validation/artifact contract are registered.
Do not omit unit metadata from model parameters or energy outputs.
Do not treat distance-only periodic completion as sufficient for decorated lattices such as dice.

Model Hamiltonian Operations.summary: Planner operations are controlled edits over a base model input.

sections.heading: Target Fields
items: Use site: 3 for one integer site ID and sites: [0, 2] for a list of integer site IDs. The shared operation engine applies grouped sites directly; splitting into single-site operations is unnecessary.
A template reference in site must resolve to one integer; use sites for a reference that resolves to a group. A list in site is invalid and must not be flattened or reduced to its first element.
Use bond: 7 for one bond ID, bonds: [2, 7] for bond IDs, and bond: [0, 2] for endpoint site IDs. Do not confuse site IDs with bond IDs.

sections.heading: Allowed Operation Types
items: `change_nelec`: change spin-resolved electron count.
`set_site_parameter`: change onsite energy or Hubbard U on selected sites.
`set_bond_parameter`: change hopping t or interaction V on selected bonds.
`sweep`: produce cases over a numeric range.
`case_design`: produce an explicit list of cases such as defects or dopings.

sections.heading: Validation
items: Reject unknown operation names.
Reject site or bond indices not present in the input file.
Reject ambiguous parameter names.
Normalize electron-count operations before case generation.
Use capability-registry parameter scopes to decide whether a parameter is valid for site, bond, global, or sweep usage.
Do not expose internal effective_t/effective_V fields as planner sweep parameters unless the registry explicitly marks them sweep-capable.

sections.heading: Rule
items: `nelec` at execution boundary must be a two-item list or tuple: `[nalpha, nbeta]`.
For total electron count N: if N is even, use `[N/2, N/2]`; if N is odd, use `[(N+1)/2, (N-1)/2]` unless the user specifies spin differently.
Validate `0 <= nalpha <= norb` and `0 <= nbeta <= norb`.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not pass scalar total electron counts to `change_nelec`.
Do not infer high-spin alternatives unless the user asks for them.
Do not execute if electron count exceeds orbital capacity.

sections.heading: Failure Example
items: Bad: `{"op":"change_nelec","nelec":3}`.
Good: `{"op":"change_nelec","nelec":[2,1]}`.

Builder Navigation and Messaging Contrac.summary: Builder navigation is a UI/browser handoff protocol, not a scientific model schema.

sections.heading: Message Schema
items: Builder save messages must include target, work directory, saved input path, and lightweight model metadata for UI preview.
Target identifies whether the receiver is the single agent or planner agent.
Caller surfaces must update their model input state from the returned path.

sections.heading: Navigation Rule
items: Open builder in a named window or tab when caller state must be preserved.
Back-to-web-UI actions must notify the opener instead of reloading and losing state.
If the opener is unavailable, show the saved path and let the user manually return.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not use download-only builder output for agent integration.
Do not route planner builder output to the single-agent state or vice versa.
Do not refresh the agent/planner page on return.

Molecular Method Selection Rules.summary: Molecular calculations must use normalized method, reference, charge, and spin settings.

sections.heading: Capability Matrix
items: `hf`: Hartree-Fock; omit `xc`; validate RHF/UHF/ROHF reference.
`dft`: density functional theory; require `xc`; validate RKS/UKS reference.
`mp2`: post-HF method requiring a converged HF reference.
`ccsd`: coupled-cluster method requiring a compatible HF reference.
`ccsd_t`: CCSD plus perturbative triples for a weak single-reference regime.
`fci`: Full CI using orbitals from mean-field setup; prefer small systems by default.
`casci` and `casscf`: approved active-space methods; SC-NEVPT2 is a restricted ground-state post-CAS correction.

sections.heading: Method Rules
items: Hartree-Fock is represented as `hf` and must omit `xc`; non-DFT methods normalize empty `xc` to null.
DFT requires an exchange-correlation functional such as B3LYP.
Post-Hartree-Fock methods require a valid mean-field reference.
MP2, CC, CI, FCI, and CAS must be validated against closed-shell/open-shell support.
CASSCF/CASCI require explicit approved ncas/nelecas; do not silently choose an ambiguous active space.

Explicit molecular density fitting supports scf_and_casscf for restricted/ROHF CASSCF with FCI or block2; legacy scf scope on restricted CASSCF normalizes to that combined scope. Results report actual applied_to and the optimizer implementation. Unrestricted DF-CASSCF and DF active two-electron integrals in block2 CASCI are unsupported.

block2 CAS defaults solver.options.mpo_algorithm to conventional; fast_bipartite remains an explicit option and saved explicit selections are retained. Conventional uses NC for two orbitals and defaults integral_cutoff to 1e-12 (FastBipartite: 1e-20). This integral-screening threshold differs from DMRG truncation cutoff. Effective settings and MPO/sweep/RDM timings are recorded. Small fixed-orbital checks against FCI and official dmrgscf/block2main pass. The lutein M=600 Amarel comparison observed about 55% lower custom-process peak RSS and only 2.3% shorter median time with Conventional over two repeats; all paths remained unconverged. This does not establish a general speedup. Active-space Boys/PM supports explicit orbital_processing.localization_occupation_thresholds: [] preserves whole-block localization, [1.0] separates low/high reference occupations, and [0.1, 1.9] defines three groups. Diagonalize the spin-summed SCF density projected into the selected active block, then localize each interval independently; no 2-RDM is required. Boundaries are strictly increasing inside (0,2), with equality in the lower interval. Record occupations, group membership and preserved-subspace checks in cas_result.orbital_provenance. Fiedler ordering is separate. This changes only the initial orbital basis, not active-space membership or subsequent CASSCF rotations; compatible joint restarts retain their saved basis. In the lutein fixed-CAS(20e,20o), M=600 pilot, whole PM+Fiedler and split PM+Fiedler both met DMRG criteria while whole PM without reordering did not. Whole PM+Fiedler was slightly lower in energy and faster in that single comparison; keep split localization optional and do not infer CASSCF orbital convergence from this fixed-orbital result.

MolecularCorrelationRisk preserves separate physics, solver-stress, overall diagnostic, and routing levels. Nonconvergence raises the overall diagnostic warning without rewriting physical evidence; solver stress alone need not trigger multireference promotion.
T1 >= 0.05 or D1 >= 0.10 is the current CCSD policy threshold for multireference review, not a universal accuracy cutoff. Ground-state SC-NEVPT2 requires an approved spin-adapted CAS and root 0.

Restricted/ROHF CASSCF with FCI or block2 accepts orbital_processing.frozen_orbital_indices (default []). These are reviewed, unique zero-based full MO indices after active-space preparation, recorded in cas_result.orbital_optimization. Explicitly frozen external virtuals are omitted from the internal MO integral workspace; all occupied and active MOs remain with their requested PySCF frozen constraints. Checkpoints and output arrays restore the complete MO layout, and integral_space records the working-to-full mapping. AO integrals and J/K operations retain the full AO basis. Freezing holds orbital coefficients fixed without reducing the AO basis or changing the CAS electron count. Inactive double occupancy alone is not orbital freezing. No automatic chemical-core count or virtual-energy cutoff is assumed.

sections.heading: Reference Rules
items: Ordinary closed-shell single-reference methods default to restricted references. Automatic CAS uses a UHF orbital probe followed by shared spatial orbitals and spin-adapted RHF/ROHF CAS; initial_reference and cas_reference are distinct.
Open-shell systems default to unrestricted or ROHF only when supported by the selected method.
A user-provided reference override wins after validation.
Model Hamiltonian mean-field-based solvers default to unrestricted references; do not apply the molecular closed-shell default to half-filled model systems.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not leave stale DFT defaults when the user switches to Hartree-Fock.
Do not run post-HF without a compatible mean-field object.
Do not let UI method labels diverge from the normalized backend task spec.

sections.heading: Validated Lutein Boundary (September 21)
items: The September 20–21 lutein follow-up achieved converged M=600 orbital optimization with PM+Fiedler and Conventional MPO. A separate fixed-orbital M=2000 solve does not establish M=2000-optimized CASSCF. With 42 frozen core orbitals, the full external-space result shifted by 0.0248 mHa from the preceding unfrozen result. Initial +3/+5 eV external virtual windows failed the agreed 0.1 mHa energy and 0.01 NOON-difference targets despite inner/orbital convergence. Compressed and original MO workspaces agreed within 8e-10 Ha at the same frozen constraints. These are case-specific observations, not automatic core/window defaults. AO DF storage remains full-size, so fewer working MOs do not imply proportionally lower peak RSS. See the September 21 overnight-results report.

Model Hamiltonian Solver Support.summary: Model-Hamiltonian solver choice is separate from model structure.

sections.heading: Supported Solver Values
items: `mp2`: model-Hamiltonian MP2.
`ccsd`: model-Hamiltonian CCSD.
`ccsd_t`: model-Hamiltonian CCSD(T).
`fci`: finite-model Full CI; requested spectrum/strong-correlation diagnostics use complete dense diagonalization up to determinant dimension 5,000.
`block2_dmrg`: optional finite-cluster DMRG with structured sweeps, RDM observables, entanglement, low roots, symmetry checks, and checkpoint manifests.
`dmet`: optional self-consistent libDMET for supported single-band Hubbard clusters; `solver.options.impurity_solver` selects `fci`, `ccsd`, or `block2_dmrg` inside the DMET loop.
`tight_binding`: backend-only primitive-cell one-body Bloch solver for h(k), bands, DOS, filling, and k-mesh occupations; nonzero U/V are recorded but not applied.

sections.heading: DMET Execution Mode
items: DMET with intersite V requires solver.options.execution_mode=finite_graph to preserve the supplied Hubbard sites, bonds, U, V, and hopping t. Explicit translational mode requires translation-equivalent primitive cells and no_intersite_interaction; uniform nonzero V also fails this check. Omitting the mode lets validation choose from the supplied graph.

Use a complete non-overlapping fragment partition for finite_graph. Keep the top-level solver dmet and select FCI, CCSD, or block2 through impurity_solver. Finite-graph partitions require nalpha=nbeta; translated representative fragments may use a validated nonzero spin sector.

sections.heading: Reference Rule
items: Mean-field-based model Hamiltonian solvers use an unrestricted reference by default.
The unrestricted reference applies to MP2, CCSD, CCSD(T), and the reference diagnostics reported alongside Full CI.
Do not reuse the molecular closed-shell default for half-filled Hubbard-like model systems.

sections.heading: Rule
items: Solver selection happens in the agent/planner layer, not in builder output.
Supported solvers must be validated through the solver capability registry.
Energy spectra must be saved for the selected method when that method produces a spectrum.
Reject any solver absent from the capability registry before execution.

Model-Hamiltonian studies retain an explicit solver under study_mode=static and may opt into grid_refinement for parameter sampling. Diagnostics do not introduce molecular initial-scan stages or automatically replace the solver. See [[Model Grid Convergence Barriers]].
Failed or unconverged solver output is strong solver-stress evidence with a preserved independent physics level; blocked validation or approval is not correlation evidence.
A saved block2 MPS may seed a later task only after orbital/electron/spin/symmetry/root/ordering compatibility and executor identity are validated.
For DMET with a block2 impurity solver, keep the top-level solver as `dmet`; do not move `block2_dmrg` out of `solver.options.impurity_solver`.

sections.heading: DMET Convergence And Result Quality
items: Reject top-level DMET solver.options keys absent from the Registry contract, including misspelled tolerances and unregistered conv_tol; do not silently retain them while executing default settings. Nested impurity options keep their provider-specific validation.

DMET convergence requires energy change and consecutive mean-field 1RDM change to meet energy_tolerance and density_tolerance. density_fit_tolerance defines an optional density-fit diagnostic; correlation-potential change is also diagnostic. Neither residual is a required outer-convergence gate.

DMET correlation-potential fitting must use the same Hamiltonian as lattice mean field in all fitting routes, regardless of the impurity solver. Preserve the physical Fock for interacting baths; cell-local HF potentials use the k-averaged density. This density-matrix fit is separate from molecular auxiliary-basis density fitting.

Outer DMET convergence is separate from lattice and impurity SCF convergence. CCSD preliminary RHF/UHF uses native PySCF ADIIS/CDIIS. impurity_solver_options.beta defaults to 1000 and is shared by preliminary impurity SCF, lattice mean-field and density fitting; explicit omission resolves to that default. It must be positive and finite. Correlated CCSD retains integer electron counts and is not finite-temperature CCSD. The adapter stops before CCSD if preliminary SCF fails convergence or gradient checks, and records SCF calls and final CCSD/lambda convergence. FCI and block2 retain the existing mean-field/density-fit beta policy.

Calculation Assistant and Study Planner show the optional CCSD Impurity SCF beta field only for DMET with CCSD. Blank omits beta; a positive value reaches the same nested solver option. Task snapshots and saved Study plans retain it, and switching impurity solvers excludes the CCSD beta. Result summaries use recorded SCF beta rather than inventing values for legacy reports.

For a reported linear algebra failure specifically in preliminary impurity SCF DIIS, prepare a selected-case retry with solver.options.impurity_scf_diis=false (default true), available for native FCI/CCSD only. Preserve the model and tolerances; do not repeat this change if already applied. Run Plan executes the reviewed subset through the existing Study agent. runtime.max_cycle does not control DMET; max_iterations controls the outer loop, and solver_max_cycle controls the correlated impurity solver.

Fractional occupations use the libDMET eigenvalue bath with a validated fixed valence sector; idempotent references obtain the impurity electron count from the projected density trace, including collapsed baths in the atomic limit.

DMET and block2 report quality_checks observations, operators, limits, and sources. The task execution-quality gate evaluates them independently: required convergence failures request review, while failed or malformed constraints block eligibility.

Declared quality checks require non-null observed evidence. equal requires compatible boolean, string, or finite numeric observed/expected values; booleans are not numbers. Numeric threshold operators require finite numeric observed/limit values, and malformed evidence is invalid. Optional checks remain advisory.

Study rows retain raw results and carry quality_status and publication_eligible. Legacy results without declared quality evidence remain displayable with legacy status and publication_eligible=null; execution success alone does not establish scientific quality.

publication_eligible=true covers the registered per-run checks only; it does not establish multi-iteration stability, bidirectional-scan agreement, fragment-size convergence, or finite-size convergence.

sections.heading: DMET Density Continuation And Spin Baths
items: bath_spin_dimension_policy defaults to native. Explicit max completes the smaller spin eigenvalue bath while preserving native selected modes; require finite_graph with a noninteracting bath. SVD baths stay native. Record per-fragment counts and orthogonality diagnostics; do not rescale density or electron counts.

reference_density_source transfers the final mean-field 1RDM from a converged compatible donor, pinned by Run and checksum. Only U/V may differ; target auxiliary u starts at zero. Never substitute an initial seed or correlated density. See [[DMET Density Continuation And Branch Analysis]].

Use analyze_dmet_branches for saved candidate minima and final-order classification. prepare_dmet_continuation previews a bounded branch sweep; start_dmet_continuation executes its saved action. Seed names do not certify phases, failed retries do not erase historical candidates, and missing donors cause skips.

sections.heading: Output Rule
items: Use human-readable `.txt` spectra with tab-separated columns.
Label energies with the input unit, such as `a.u.`.
Keep registered structured JSON plus plotting-ready TSV artifacts for spectra and Bloch outputs.
Persist model strong-correlation diagnostics as a dedicated versioned artifact, not only inside the compact comparison row.

Strong Correlation Roadmap Rules.summary: Use implemented correlation diagnostics within their molecular or finite-model scope; separate routing heuristics, numerical recovery, and future capabilities.

sections.heading: Molecular Diagnostics And Routing
items: MolecularCorrelationRisk reports physics_level, solver_stress_level, overall diagnostic level, and routing_level separately. Nonconvergence raises the overall warning, not necessarily the physical evidence or the next-method route; blocked input is not correlation evidence.

Current scores and thresholds are heuristic policy. confidence counts available evidence components; it is not a calibrated probability or energy-error estimate. See [[Correlation Diagnostic Interpretation]].
Adaptive initial strategies auto, mp2, and fci apply to molecular studies. Auto uses the shared Registry probe; refinement preserves the requested final CAS method and solver settings.

Current molecular routing proposes CCSD(T) in weak regions, CCSD in moderate regions, and reviewed CAS candidates for strong physical evidence. Solver stress alone can route through CCSD; failed CCSD(T) retries with CCSD before CAS promotion. These choices do not guarantee a monotonic improvement in energy accuracy.

Active-space proposals need their orbital/density provenance and explicit review. UNO uses the spin-summed 1-RDM; SCF stability is opt-in. Matching CAS dimensions across cases does not establish matching orbital character.

sections.heading: Static Model Studies
items: Model-Hamiltonian studies execute a static full-grid scan with the explicitly selected solver. There is no model initial-scan or molecular ActiveSpaceAudit stage, and diagnostics do not silently replace the solver.

strong_correlation_diagnostics records finite-cluster evidence. FCI or block2 may provide targeted roots, double occupancy, spin/charge correlations and RDMs within their registered scopes; finite-size evidence alone is not a thermodynamic phase claim.
Complete-spectrum FCI diagnostics require dense diagonalization, cost review, and the registered determinant limit (currently 5,000). Targeted roots do not imply a complete spectrum.

Reference-relative correlation energy is internal bookkeeping, not a public result or plot field. Do not expose screening_energy as a physical observable; show final energy, solver, filling, gap, supported diagnostic scalars, and status.

sections.heading: Recovery And Interpretation
items: Failed cases require an observed cause and a registered case-specific recovery action. Reviewed retries retain Study and case IDs, create a new Run, and preserve the full report; Status and Collect do not submit retries.

block2 recovery considers sweep-energy change and discarded weight separately. The Registry automatic-recovery budget currently caps escalation at M=1024; explicit calculations may use larger M. This budget is not a scientific convergence threshold.
A final fixed-orbital DMRG solve at larger M does not reoptimize CASSCF orbitals at that M. In-space entanglement cannot establish completeness of the active space.

DMET outer convergence and impurity convergence are separate evidence. Review a DIIS-specific failure through the supported impurity_scf_diis option, not generic SCF cycle changes. A completed job is not a calibrated physical accuracy result.

sections.heading: Capability Boundaries
items: Restricted/ROHF DF-CASSCF with FCI or block2, same-sector state-averaged CASSCF, and registered fcDMFT periodic G0W0/HF+DMFT/GW+DMFT single-task routes are executable within Registry and provider restrictions.
Unrestricted DMRG-CASSCF, unrestricted AVAS, ab initio DMET, AFQMC, different-spin state averaging, excited-root SC-NEVPT2, periodic MP2/CC, and periodic Planner scans remain future integrations.

Finite Hubbard libDMET is a model solver; molecular DMET-CAS guesses and first-principles crystalline DMET are different capabilities. Do not infer support from a PySCF API name or from the presence of a DMFT provider.

Diagnostic calibration and reference-error/cost comparisons are proposed validation work. Existing regression benchmarks do not establish learned weights, universal strong-correlation thresholds, or guaranteed method-selection accuracy.

Task Specification Contract.summary: The task spec is the canonical execution request schema.

sections.heading: Required Common Fields
items: `task_type`: molecular, model_hamiltonian, or periodic.
`system`: normalized molecular geometry, basis, charge, spin, and unit for molecular tasks.
`method` or `solver`: canonical calculation target after normalization.
`runtime`: explicit iteration and convergence settings.
`analysis`: requested outputs plus generated workflow diagnostics.

sections.heading: Molecular Spec Fields
items: `system.atom`.
`basis`.
`charge`.
`spin`.
`method`: canonical value such as `hf`, `dft`, `mp2`, `ccsd`, `ccsd_t`, `fci`, `casci`, or `casscf`.
`xc` only when method is DFT.
`restricted`: true, false, or automatic after validation.
`active_space` and `post_cas` when a CAS workflow is requested.

sections.heading: Model-Hamiltonian Spec Fields
items: `model_hamiltonian.input_file` or normalized `model_hamiltonian.spec`.
`solver`: canonical model-Hamiltonian solver.
`nelec`: spin-resolved `[nalpha, nbeta]`.
`analysis.outputs`: registered model outputs.
Planner operations: optional validated edits applied to case copies.

sections.heading: Periodic Spec Fields
items: `periodic.structure_text` and `structure_format`: POSCAR or CIF input.
Registered periodic Gaussian basis and GTH pseudopotential for every element.
HF/DFT method, XC only for DFT, charge/spin/reference, regular k mesh, numerical controls, PBC density fitting, exxdiv, and optional smearing.
Optional ASE, SeeK-path, validated standard-label, or explicit-coordinate band-path contract.
Periodic tasks are executable in the Calculation Assistant but remain planner-disallowed.

sections.heading: Execution Metadata
items: Execution target and resource-profile ids are transport metadata outside the scientific task specification.
Named remote profiles select server-owned Slurm settings; they must not rewrite method, solver, charge, spin, or active-space fields.

sections.heading: Active-Space Probe
items: An automatic active-space request may execute an MP2 probe before the target CAS calculation.
The probe contract records the eventual CASCI/CASSCF target method, target solver, and target solver options.
Approval restores target fields; MP2 and probe-only requirements must not appear as the formal target method or solver.

sections.heading: SCF Recovery
items: An automatic molecular reference retry preserves the requested SCF algorithm and doubles the cycle limit. Newton is an explicit runtime.scf_algorithm=newton choice, not an automatic fallback. With an unchanged reference policy, recovery uses the latest attempt's one_particle_state.data_artifact through initial_state.mode=projected_1rdm and PySCF's native dm0 input.
An unfinished reference density retains scf_converged=false; the restart report records initial_state.source_scf_converged. A restart guess is not an accepted scientific result.

Changing restricted/unrestricted policy clears incompatible restart data. A missing latest artifact does not select an older attempt. Density restart does not restore DIIS/Newton history or DF integral caches.

Automatic retries use structured convergence state, preserve the reference choice, and record both the previous and retry task specification. Error-message substrings do not authorize retries; DMET outer-loop failures do not trigger generic SCF-cycle changes.

sections.heading: UI Synchronization Rule
items: The UI must reflect task-spec changes in real time.
When the user changes method, solver, basis, charge, spin, reference, nelec, or input path, the canonical task spec must update immediately.
Execution buttons must read from the canonical task spec, not from stale UI defaults.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not start execution from an unconfirmed structure draft.
Do not keep duplicate default values that can override user edits.
Do not treat `verbose` or display preferences as scientific method changes unless wired to backend behavior.

sections.heading: Optional Stability And UNO Candidates
items: SCF stability runs only when workflow.module_config["molecular.correlation_diagnostics"].scf_stability=true. The default reports not_requested with stable=null and contributes no stability score.
A UHF occupation-window candidate without correlated occupations uses eigenvectors of the spin-summed AO 1-RDM in the overlap metric. It requires no correlated 2-RDM or SCF stability check.
Preserve actual UNO occupations and the full core-active-virtual initial_mo_coeff for approval and execution. Canonical orbital indices in a projected candidate are display mappings only.

sections.heading: CAS Starting Reference
items: CASCI/CASSCF uses an initial UHF reference even when method.restricted=true selects a spin-adapted CAS formulation. Portable one-particle-state metadata and restart compatibility follow the actual initial SCF policy, allowing a saved UHF probe density to seed CAS.

sections.heading: DMRG-CASSCF Precision And Cost
items: solver.options.mpo_algorithm defaults to conventional; fast_bipartite remains an explicit option. Existing saved requests keep explicitly recorded settings. Conventional uses NC for two active orbitals. An omitted integral_cutoff resolves to 1e-12 for Conventional or 1e-20 for FastBipartite; this screens integrals, unlike the DMRG truncation cutoff. Results record the effective choice and MPO/sweep/RDM timings, including per-call CASSCF traces. The fixed-orbital H6 official-interface comparison validates numerical agreement, not lutein speedup. Active-space Boys/PM supports explicit orbital_processing.localization_occupation_thresholds: [] preserves whole-block localization, [1.0] separates low/high reference occupations, and [0.1, 1.9] defines three groups. Diagonalize the spin-summed SCF density projected into the selected active block, then localize each interval independently; no 2-RDM is required. Boundaries are strictly increasing inside (0,2), with equality in the lower interval. Record occupations, group membership and preserved-subspace checks in cas_result.orbital_provenance. Fiedler ordering is separate. This changes only the initial orbital basis, not active-space membership or subsequent CASSCF rotations; compatible joint restarts retain their saved basis. In the lutein fixed-CAS(20e,20o), M=600 pilot, whole PM+Fiedler and split PM+Fiedler both met DMRG criteria while whole PM without reordering did not. Whole PM+Fiedler was slightly lower in energy and faster in that single comparison; keep split localization optional and do not infer CASSCF orbital convergence from this fixed-orbital result.

Task orbital settings are resolved before provider defaults; explicit solver options and then workflow-module overrides take precedence. Preserve requested options even when the local optional provider is unavailable.

bond_dimensions controls orbital-optimization DMRG calls; final_bond_dimension requests a separate fixed-orbital solve after optimization. Both use the configured sweeps limit. A larger final M does not establish orbital convergence at that M, and exact-sector planning can cap the effective M below the request.
Inspect solver-call role, effective M, actual fixed permutation, energy change, discarded weight and orbital convergence separately. Cancelled orbital optimization has no final fixed-orbital result.

A smaller CAS leaves the AO basis and most inactive/external orbital rotations in place. DF JK orbital response can dominate runtime; use small molecules for cheap workflow tests rather than assuming a small CAS makes a large molecule inexpensive.

UNO and AVAS initial_mo_coeff accepts inline matrices or pyscf-agent.numeric-array.v1 references with NPY path, shape and dtype. Full guesses above 4096 elements are externalized before workflow/history and new Study execution copies; CAS loads only the referenced array. SSH stages local numerical artifacts and rewrites paths. Existing DMRG/DMET and AO 1RDM NPZ formats remain unchanged. This is storage support, not cross-geometry orbital projection.

Restricted/ROHF CASSCF with FCI or block2 accepts orbital_processing.frozen_orbital_indices (default []). These are reviewed, unique zero-based full MO indices after active-space preparation, recorded in cas_result.orbital_optimization. Explicitly frozen external virtuals are omitted from the internal MO integral workspace; all occupied and active MOs remain with their requested PySCF frozen constraints. Checkpoints and output arrays restore the complete MO layout, and integral_space records the working-to-full mapping. AO integrals and J/K operations retain the full AO basis. Freezing holds orbital coefficients fixed without reducing the AO basis or changing the CAS electron count. Inactive double occupancy alone is not orbital freezing. No automatic chemical-core count or virtual-energy cutoff is assumed.

sections.heading: Input Normalization
items: Missing fields may receive documented defaults. Explicit malformed values, non-finite numbers, fractional integers, and unknown execution-request fields are validation errors, not requests for defaults.
Lossless scalar aliases and equivalent geometry formats may normalize at the shared contract boundary. Report readers accept additive fields without treating invalid owned values as defaults.
Validate provider-owned options before execution. Block2 presets and bounded automatic recovery policy come from the capability registry.

sections.heading: Canonical Runtime And Provider Settings
items: Density-fitting shorthand aliases density_fit, df, auxbasis, df_auxbasis and density_fitting_auxbasis remain supported. Orbital orders use lossless integer conversion and cannot truncate fractional entries.

Finite-model reference SCF consumes TaskSpec runtime through dispatch and generated input. Defaults are max_cycle=50 and upstream PySCF tolerance when conv_tol is absent; reproduce the former implicit 200/1e-10 policy only by requesting those values explicitly. DMET reference controls remain provider-owned.

Study max-cycle recovery consumes shorthand runtime aliases before updating the canonical runtime object. Model reference multi-start records each attempt and error; the site-index guesses are bounded heuristics, not a general graph-sublattice construction.

Block2 orbital-only restart manifests and provenance survive option validation and normalization. Costing resolves provider presets and labels its estimate as the initial DMRG schedule, excluding adaptive extensions, final solves and CASSCF macroiterations.

Run Directory Artifact Storage.summary: Run directories persist registered, versioned scientific evidence while workflow state carries compact artifact references.

sections.heading: Must
items: Create one canonical work directory for a single submitted task unless the planner intentionally creates multiple case directories.

Store generated input files, stdout logs, structured results, molecular correlation/ActiveSpaceAudit/CAS results, block2 DMRG results and bond-dimension plans, model spectra/diagnostics/Bloch outputs, periodic structures/numerics/orbitals/bands, study checkpoints/reports, and plot data under registered artifact contracts.
Every artifact reference carries kind, path, size_bytes, mime_type, and description.

Versioned JSON payloads use their registered schemas, including study-plan, cost-estimate, study-state, study-report, adaptive decision/report, molecular/model diagnostic, block2 result/bond-dimension/CASSCF/MPS, Bloch, periodic, and plot-data schemas.
Keep root RDMs and entanglement matrices in registered binary artifacts when they are too large for compact task reports.
Use semantic filenames that distinguish input, result, log, and artifact roles; dynamic per-observable files match `observable-*`.

Persist the last finite molecular SCF density as a one_particle_state binary artifact, even when unconverged. Record scf_converged and the exact data_artifact reference; keep density arrays out of compact reports and prompts.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not expose internal attempt labels in user-facing names unless retry semantics matter.
Do not create multiple work directories for one single calculation.
Do not store long artifacts only inside workflow state.
Do not emit an unregistered artifact kind or return a path-only reference without integrity metadata.
Do not replace a merged full adaptive report with a one-case recovery report.

Backend Normalization for Electron Count.summary: Scalar electron-count requests caused planner failures; backend normalization is mandatory.

sections.heading: Symptom
items: Planner repeatedly fails with `change_nelec requires a two-item nelec list`.
User states a total electron range, but generated operations keep scalar electron counts.

sections.heading: Root Cause
items: The LLM interpreted total electron count as execution-ready `nelec`.
Validation expected spin-resolved electron counts.

sections.heading: Permanent Rule
items: Normalize total electron count to `[nalpha, nbeta]` before validation reaches execution.
Even total N maps to `[N/2, N/2]`; odd total N maps to `[(N+1)/2, (N-1)/2]` unless user specifies otherwise.

sections.heading: Regression Test
items: Generate a campaign from total electrons 1 to 15 and assert every case has a two-item `nelec` list.
Run the validator on odd and even electron counts before invoking PySCF.

Reproducibility Failure Pattern: Hidden.summary: Repeated submissions must not produce different results from mutated hidden defaults.

sections.heading: Symptom
items: The same calculation submitted twice gives different energies.
The second run matches expectation while the first run used stale or mutated defaults.

sections.heading: Root Cause
items: UI state, hidden planner state, and serialized input file diverged.
Preparation mutated defaults that were not written back into the normalized spec.

sections.heading: Permanent Rule
items: Before execution, serialize a normalized model or molecular spec and execute only that spec.
Display the active spec or preview derived from the same serialized data.
Treat first-run vs second-run mismatch as a regression failure.

sections.heading: Regression Test
items: Run the same submitted task twice from a fresh page state.
Assert identical normalized specs, generated inputs, and energies within numerical tolerance.

Model Hamiltonian Builder State Loss.summary: Builder return navigation must preserve caller state and saved model input.

sections.heading: Symptom
items: Back-to-web-UI refreshes the page and loses selected work directory, model path, or planner conversation.
Builder output appears in the wrong surface.

sections.heading: Permanent Rule
items: Use named-window or opener messaging patterns for multi-page workflows.
Return saved input path and target identifier through `postMessage`.
Keep a manual fallback path visible when opener communication fails.

sections.heading: Regression Test
items: Open builder from agent and planner surfaces, save input, return, and assert caller state is preserved.
Verify target routing prevents cross-surface state pollution.

Scan Path Continuity Diagnostics.summary: Scan-path continuity is an explicit result-analysis capability; Run Plan leaves case calculations independent.

sections.heading: Detection Rule
items: Run the check only after the user selects Analyze Results; do not inspect neighboring cases or reuse their density matrices during normal adaptive execution.
Apply only to completed one-dimensional scans with at least four successful energy points and exactly one numeric scan coordinate.
Flag a boundary only when adjacent points use different methods and the transition slope disagrees with neighboring same-method slopes beyond both a relative and energy-residual threshold.
Check one-sided endpoint risks separately and treat every finding as a numerical-routing quality signal, not a thermodynamic phase classifier or proof that a single-point diagnostic is wrong.

sections.heading: Refinement Rule
items: First retry the flagged local window in both coordinate directions without changing target methods, using compatible AO 1RDM artifacts from adjacent tasks.
Require explicit review for endpoint validation and cross-method or cross-reference seeds; accept replacement results only when both branches converge and agree.
Promote the overlap window to CASSCF only when continuation cannot establish a consistent branch.
Create a separate plan-scoped ActiveSpaceAudit batch for the affected overlap region; do not silently run the promoted calculation.
Merge approved local results back into the parent adaptive report before plotting or interpreting the full curve.

sections.heading: Artifact Rule
items: Normal adaptive execution writes `scan-path-diagnostics.json` with status `deferred` and schema `pyscf-agent.scan-path-diagnostics.v1`.
After explicit analysis, store diagnostics, paired continuation plans and validation when used, or an `adaptive-path-refinement-plan` when method promotion is needed.

Capability Registry Runtime Boundary.summary: The registry owns executable capability facts and flow semantics, not presentation details.

sections.heading: Owns
items: Capability family and canonical id.
Execution status: executable, design_only, planned, or reference_only.
Planner and backend allow flags.
Runtime limitations that affect validation or planning.
Calculation-flow semantics such as model-Hamiltonian parameter scopes: site, bond, global, and sweep.
Registered workflow modules and roles, including active-space probes that prepare evidence without activating a target solver.

Canonical study modes, adaptive initial-scan strategies and aliases, workflow options, artifact kinds/patterns, payload schemas, execution-target capabilities, public resource-profile ids, and cross-module resource limits.

sections.heading: Does Not Own
items: UI labels, layout, colors, button text, or helper copy.
Long scientific explanations that belong in wiki source pages.
Generated capability tables that can be recreated from code.
Private SSH credentials and raw server queue, CPU, memory, or wall-time values.
Browser-only UI state or test fixtures.

sections.heading: Boundary Rule
items: Backend constants and planner capability snapshots derive from the registry.
UI adapters may derive option ids from the registry but own display labels.
Wiki pages may explain rationale and roadmap, but runtime code must not depend on compiled wiki output to decide executability.
Registry metadata must stay runtime-oriented; reject presentation-only keys such as ui_label.
Probe modules identify their probe method and preserve target method, solver, and solver options in a structured contract.
Calculation Assistant active-space selection always uses the canonical auto probe; only the Planner exposes auto, mp2, and fci initial-scan strategies.
Serialize canonical adaptive ids `auto`, `mp2`, and `fci`; reject removed strategy ids and legacy solver fields instead of changing workflow semantics.
Artifact audit tests must ensure every writer kind or dynamic pattern is registered and every declared payload schema is actually written.

Planner Agent Postprocessing.summary: Registered Study postprocessing provides plots, exact plotted data, dataset exports and energy-stratified trajectory geometry selection.

sections.heading: Built-In Tools
items: `line_plot`, `scatter_plot`, `bar_plot`, and `heatmap` are the current built-in postprocessing tools.
Supported postprocessing tool ids are runtime capabilities and should derive from the capability registry.
Tool labels and UI presentation stay in UI adapters.

sections.heading: Dataset Actions
items: generate_hamiltonian_dataset and collect_hamiltonian_dataset are separate registered postprocessing actions, not plot tools; see [[Molecular Hamiltonian Dataset Workflow]].
