Finalization creates lightweight sample/rejection indexes without downloading remote NPZ files. Generation materializes and validates a portable dataset on the selected execution target and returns a receipt.
Collection requires successful generation and transfers the already generated dataset only when requested. Neither action requires content-checksum validation.
Derive trajectory/sample progress and generated/collected states from existing Study plans, receipts, and manifests rather than adding another scheduler state.

sections.heading: Energy-Stratified Trajectory Selection
items: Use registered postprocessing.action select_energy_stratified_frames to choose a labeling subset from accepted MD trajectories. It is owned by study.postprocessing and runs through the existing Study postprocessing API; the WebUI exposes Select by Energy.

Pass count_per_molecule (required), time_start_fs (default 0), and time_end_fs (default null) in the action object. Each molecule is filtered by the inclusive time window, sorted by potential energy then frame index and sample ID, divided into equal-population energy bins (larger bins first), and represented by the lower median frame of each bin.

Read only the accepted sample JSONL index, retaining geometry, energy, split and provenance; never load trajectory Fock/overlap arrays or call an LLM. The index must be accessible where postprocessing runs. Use provenance.time_au or the declared fixed MD timestep times frame_index for physical time.

HamiltonianSample.total_energy_hartree means MD potential energy, not potential plus nuclear kinetic energy. Export registered selection-manifest JSON, selected-frames JSONL and Angstrom XYZ with source identities. Original trajectories and dataset splits remain unchanged; no CCSD is submitted.

If a molecule has fewer candidates than requested, record the shortage and select none for it. Preserve visibility of source rejections and missing molecules; do not duplicate frames or claim a complete campaign. A time cutoff is an explicit sampling choice, not proof of equilibration; the selected frames are not guaranteed independent.

sections.heading: Plot Rules
items: Use matplotlib and a consistent publication-oriented style.
Plot specs use comparison-table columns, not hardcoded domain names.
Users must be able to choose x and y fields from available case variables and numeric result columns.

For model Hamiltonian studies, numeric result columns may include final_energy, correlation_energy, filling, gap, mean_field_gap, natural_occupation_fractionality, fractional_natural_orbital_count, and max_double_excitation_amplitude when present.
Each generated plot writes `plot-<name>.png`, `.spec.json`, `.data.tsv`, and `.data.json` under a shared prefix.
Expose plotted TSV/JSON data with the figure; do not surface plot-spec JSON as the sole primary artifact.
Plot only the merged full adaptive report, not an isolated recovery subset.

Built-in plots exclude rows with publication_eligible=false and report excluded_case_ids; preserve the original rows and their quality evidence for review. An all-ineligible report skips plotting, while explicit dataset actions keep their separate eligibility checks.
Plot artifacts use the common kind/path/size/MIME/description reference contract, and JSON spec/data payloads carry registered schemas.
PostprocessContext owns eligible rows and column choices; WebUI consumes that projection. Explicit failed statuses exclude legacy rows with missing publication flags.
Use cell or actual TaskSpec units; leave unknown units unlabeled and reject mixed/partly unknown units. Do not silently convert or relabel values.
Validate explicit plot fields, group columns, positive integer DPI, finite figure sizes and heatmap center before rendering. Selected outputs must have distinct names.
Render and export the same numeric rows; retain excluded case ids and reasons for missing numeric/group values in response and data JSON.

sections.heading: Result Analysis Boundary
items: Run Plan produces independent case results and records scan-path analysis as deferred.
Analyze Results explicitly compares cases, runs path-continuity diagnostics, and may offer a reviewed 1RDM continuation or local method-refinement plan.
Do not launch cross-case calculations merely because an adaptive run completed.
Optional language analysis sends only contracts for actual result fields/artifact kinds, scoped by known system type, once in the user payload. The complete output catalog is not prompt context.
Keep scientific comparison rows complete. Optional feedback shares context selection and records failures without changing calculation results; do not apply language-specific reply filtering.

sections.heading: Heatmap Rules
items: Two-dimensional grid sweeps may produce heatmaps.
Heatmap specs use x and y for plane coordinates and color for the plotted numeric observable.
Use a red-blue diverging colorbar with zero fixed as the white midpoint.
Require at least two varying case variables and a numeric observable column before suggesting a heatmap.
Require unique numeric x/y coordinates for one selected series; reject duplicates and unsupported grouping rather than overwrite or average rows implicitly.

Wiki Maintenance Rules.summary: Conversation-derived rules enter the main wiki only after promotion into maintained source files.

sections.heading: Rule Inbox
items: Capture conversation-derived rules in conversation_rules first.
Promote stable rules into sources during periodic maintenance.
Keep rough, contradictory, or unreviewed notes out of sources.

sections.heading: Promotion Checklist
items: Decide whether the rule belongs in an existing source or a new source file.
Preserve the rationale or failure case when it explains why the rule exists.
Add related-page links and curated-structure entries when needed.
If a source changes runtime behavior, make sure code and tests enforce it.
Run the wiki curate/lint flow after source updates.

sections.heading: Must Not
items: Do not assume conversation_rules are available to the planner at runtime.
Do not edit generated wiki pages as the source of truth.
Do not let generated capability tables drift away from the runtime registry.

sections.heading: Publication And Retrieval
items: Maintained sources outrank historical compiler candidates and exports. pageGuidance is an explicit body override: revise it together with its source, then run wiki:curate and wiki:lint.
Use English guidance. Verify bounded retrieved passages from the packaged runtime export for changed scientific topics; do not send the whole Wiki or Registry to the LLM.

Keep executable Registry facts, heuristic interpretation, future proposals, and completed numerical evidence distinct. Runtime retrieval reads the packaged export on each call; only Python code changes require a service reload.

Molecular Hamiltonian Dataset Workflow.summary: Plan and execute QH9-compatible molecular MD datasets through existing Study cases, then finalize, generate on the execution target, and explicitly collect.

sections.heading: Executable Profile
items: One seed molecule becomes one ordinary Study case running a complete NVE trajectory; sampled frames are dataset samples, not independent scheduler cases.
Use neutral closed-shell H/C/N/O/F molecules, restricted B3LYP/def2-SVP, standard SCF, symmetry disabled, no density fitting, and no active-space/orbital-processing modules.

Select executable qh9 for reference SCF conv_tol=1e-13, or qh9_relaxed_scf for conv_tol=1e-8. Both use conv_tol_grad=3.16e-5, grid_level=3, and diis_space=8. Registry settings apply through planning, validation and execution; explicit conflicting tolerances are rejected.
Defaults are 100 molecules x 10 samples, NVE with 300 K initial velocities, time_step_au=50, steps=100, and zero-based frame indexes 9, 19, ..., 99. NVE is not thermostatted.

Sampling is independent of SCF accuracy. For the QH9-dynamic-300k sampling schedule, explicitly select time_step_au=50, steps=100, sample_stride=1, sample_offset=0, and geometries_per_molecule=100 to keep every frame. The historical default keeps only ten frames.
Preserve seed geometries, molecule/frame identities, coordinate units, and deterministic velocity seeds; retain initially unapproved Study resource review for all trajectory work.

Molecular dynamics requires explicit molecular_dynamics.profile=qh9 or qh9_relaxed_scf. Dataset planning propagates the selected compatibility_profile; standalone or saved MD requests must select it before a new execution. Generic MD requests must not silently inherit QH9 scientific settings.

sections.heading: Artifacts And Labels
items: The task kernel owns trajectory execution and QH9-ordered Fock/overlap NPZ arrays. Compact manifests preserve AO permutation/phase/atom slices, sampled geometries and energies, units, array metadata, and convergence evidence.

Integration failures preserve log-pyscf-output.log and result-molecular-md-failure.json with the failed frame, geometry, completed/retained frame counts, velocity seed, SCF convergence flag and last observed SCF residuals. Failed trajectories do not produce accepted frame arrays.

For this RKS workflow, PySCF's Gradients did not converge message reflects the underlying SCF convergence flag. Inspect the saved log before choosing recovery; max_cycle can increase without relaxing conv_tol. Retry the complete trajectory in a new Run with the original molecule and velocity seed. Failure geometry is diagnostic evidence, not a supported MD restart checkpoint.
Fock is a mean-field one-electron Hamiltonian label. It is not a full many-electron Hamiltonian; overlap and AO convention metadata must accompany it.

sections.heading: Finalize, Generate, Collect
items: Finalization writes samples.jsonl, rejections.jsonl, and dataset-manifest.json. Every expected frame must be accepted or rejected; rejected frames are not usable training samples.

Remote finalization may use self-describing report metadata without opening or downloading executor-owned arrays. A metadata manifest does not prove local availability or validate remote file contents.

generate_hamiltonian_dataset materializes and validates the portable dataset on the selected execution target, checks file presence/array keys/indexes/matrix shapes, rewrites relative matrix paths, and retains a generation receipt.
collect_hamiltonian_dataset requires successful generation and downloads that dataset only when a local copy is requested. SSH generation returns only a lightweight receipt.
Derive trajectory/sample progress and generated/collected states from the existing Study plan, receipts, and manifests; do not add another scheduler or mutable lifecycle.
Neither dataset action requires content-checksum verification. Deployment source fingerprints are a separate concern.

sections.heading: Splits And Evidence
items: Default molecule_random splitting keeps all frames of a molecule together with train/validation/test fractions 0.8/0.1/0.1 and a persisted seed. geometry_random and molecule_size_ood require explicit selection.

Record the selected profile, runtime PySCF and reference version 2.2.1, actual SCF setting deviations (empty for strict qh9), and bitwise_reproduction=false. Format/convention compatibility is not numerical reproduction.

The 100 x 10 default is a plan. One-frame numerical smoke evidence does not establish full campaign quality, trajectory energy conservation, or downstream learning accuracy; require separate acceptance records.

Installation And Remote Verification.summary: Verify package resources, public contracts, Slurm scientific results, and optional source-matched remote releases while preserving the age and scope of evidence.

sections.heading: Installation Evidence
items: verify-install checks imports outside the source checkout, distribution metadata, public schemas, entry points, Web assets, packaged Wiki, benchmark data, and lightweight scientific benchmarks.
The normal temporary environment reuses installed scientific dependencies; --wheelhouse is the isolated offline path. A passing normal wheel check does not validate isolated dependency installation.
Retain source version, environment, and date on archived evidence; the retained install.json covers 0.1.0, not current 0.2.0.

sections.heading: Remote Execution And Releases
items: SshSlurmExecutor invokes stateless RPC over SSH. Client remote.ini selects server-side profiles; the server owns cluster identity, queues, CPU, memory, wall time, and resource-profile values.
Match expected_cluster_id and the public contract before trusting the selected server. Keep connection credentials and Slurm configuration outside scientific TaskSpec payloads.
deploy-remote creates an immutable source release and private worktree binding using an existing server Python/dependency environment; it does not provision scientific dependencies.

require_runtime_match checks local source and remote environment/release/source identity and public contract. Changed deployable source, including the packaged Wiki, requires a new matching deployment; do not bypass a stale identity by disabling the check.
Deployment fingerprints are separate from scientific artifact references. Dataset generation returns a receipt; explicit collection owns transfer of the generated arrays.

sections.heading: Verification And Failures
items: verify-remote performs read-only capability/contract checks. --submit-smoke additionally requires a successful H2/HF TaskReport; --submit-batch-smoke requires exact task-id mapping, two successful reports, and scheduler artifacts.

Scheduler completion does not imply scientific success or report availability. Keep COMPLETED jobs pending collection until TaskReport is visible; never synthesize failure for a completed job during filesystem propagation. Retain structured failures for failed/cancelled jobs without dropping successful siblings.
Distinguish DNS/SSH/authentication/RPC/schema/Slurm/scientific failures and redact configured host, user, and private-key values from verification errors.
An RPC rejecting client options is a stale deployment; synchronize source rather than removing options that select the intended server.
block2 OOM/timeout may require reviewed resource-profile escalation; node failures or preemption may allow same-profile retries, while unknown failures need log inspection.
Controlled-transport regression tests do not replace live source-matched deployment, cancellation, or interrupted-resume acceptance.

DMET Density Continuation And Branch Ana.summary: Compare qualified DMET candidates and prepare bounded density-only continuation sweeps with explicit provenance.

sections.heading:
Compare Saved States

- `analyze_dmet_branches(study_id, policy=None)` analyzes saved candidates without
  submitting calculations. Use final correlated sublattice charge and magnetic
  order, never the analytic seed name, to classify each converged state.
- Default order thresholds are 0.001 on absolute sublattice half-differences.
  A 20% threshold band is ambiguous; both orders give `mixed`, neither gives
  `near_unordered`, and unavailable observations give `unknown`. Record the
  configured policy with the analysis.
- Energy comparison requires successful execution, explicit convergence,
  passed required quality checks, and finite energy per site. Missing legacy
  quality evidence is unqualified; the optional density-fit residual is not a
  veto. Compare all indexed `candidate_runs`, including historical successful
  Runs after a failed retry. Current task rows and candidate minima differ.
- Energy ties default to 1e-6 per site. Order-magnitude differences above
  `state_tolerance=0.01` mark possible hysteresis; a sign reversal alone does not.
  AFM/CDW crossings require both branches at adjacent sampled V values. Do not
  bridge missing points or label numerical failure as a physical spinodal.

## Prepare And Start A Bounded Sweep

- `prepare_dmet_continuation` saves a preview and cost estimate;
  `start_dmet_continuation` starts that saved action through the existing Study
  retry lifecycle. Preserve cost-review requirements and the saved Study revision.
- Default `mode=bidirectional` follows AFM toward increasing V and CDW toward
  decreasing V at fixed U. `mode=nearest` uses scaled U/V distance and also
  supports mixed and near-unordered branches. Automatic selection requires
  uniform U/V, inline model specs, and compatible finite-graph DMET cases.
- Select the nearest qualified compatible donor again before each step,
  including newly completed and historical Runs. Each selected physical point
  and branch receives at most one new Run per action; equivalent seed cases are
  deduplicated. Missing donors cause a recorded skip, not an analytic fallback.
- Defaults are mixing 0.2, 200 outer iterations, outer DIIS off, bath policy
  `max`, and initial auxiliary correction zero. Repeated starts of one action
  do not resubmit. After interruption, collect existing Runs before preparing
  another action. A new action can revisit points while retaining candidates.
- FCI/CCSD DMET work/memory estimates are currently unavailable; missing
  estimates are not resource upper bounds.

## Density Transfer Contract

- `solver.options.reference_density_source` names a saved `source_case_id`,
  optionally an exact `source_run_id`, or a fixed absolute artifact path and
  SHA-256. The resolved donor is pinned to its Run and `dmet_mean_field_state`.
- Transfer the full final spin-resolved mean-field 1RDM, including off-diagonal
  entries. The target rebuilds its baseline with its own Hamiltonian and starts
  auxiliary u at zero. Correlation potential, chemical potential, DIIS history,
  and impurity wavefunction are not resumed.
- Check hash, source convergence/required quality, site basis, graph, fragments,
  spin/reference, bath and impurity settings. Only U/V may differ. Require real,
  finite Hermitian density of shape `(2,nsite,nsite)`, correct spin traces, and
  occupations in [0,1] within validation tolerance; never rescale the density.
- Old Runs without the final-density artifact cannot substitute initial seeds
  or correlated embedding densities. SSH stages local artifacts with checksum
  verification; cross-server paths must already be accessible to the receiver.

Model Grid Convergence Barriers.summary: Require converged, qualified model results before further sampling and coordinate saved Studies by absolute generation.

sections.heading: Convergence Barrier Contract
items: With `grid_refinement.require_converged`, every case must succeed, explicitly converge and pass required quality checks before more sampling. Optional `convergence_retry` allows one fallback per case; a failed fallback leaves `awaiting_convergence`. A shared `grid_round_target` advances only when all grouped Studies pass the current generation. These barriers do not change the solver or transfer a donor density.

sections.heading:
Sampling And Solver Choice

- Model studies use explicit solver settings under `study_mode=static`; optional
  `grid_refinement` adapts parameter sampling. This does not enable molecular
  initial-scan method routing or active-space selection.
- `grid_refinement.require_converged` requires every current case to have
  succeeded, explicitly converged, and passed required provider quality checks
  before generating further sampling points. Missing quality evidence blocks
  the barrier. Optional density-fit diagnostics do not independently block it.

## Bounded Convergence Retry

- Optional `convergence_retry` applies one numerical fallback per case, using
  the validated mixing, iteration limit and outer-DIIS settings. The recorded
  honeycomb policy uses mixing 0.1, 400 iterations and DIIS off; those study
  settings are not universal provider defaults.
- Persist fallback overrides before submission and use them during collection
  and interrupted-receipt recovery. Preserve the canonical sampling plan,
  analytic seed, case identity, actual execution requests and previous Runs.
- This fallback transfers neither donor density nor correlation potential.
  Density continuation is a separate planned action. An unsuccessful fallback
  leaves `awaiting_convergence`; do not generate later points or retry forever.

## Shared Generation Barrier

- The application `grid_group` coordinator uses normal saved Study services.
  An absolute `grid_round_target=0` permits only seed points; each additional
  generation permits one insertion batch. Restarting a generation must not
  resubmit completed tasks.
- Grant generation N+1 only when every member has passed generation N. A member
  that reaches its sampling/budget limit remains completed while others finish.
  Errors, interrupted workers and cancellation hold the group for inspection.
- Each Study retains its own coordinator, reports, receipts and candidate
  history; the group records barriers and runs no numerical calculations.
  Different studies may choose different refined coordinates after a barrier.
- The grid group is an application coordinator, not an independently exposed
  MCP numerical solver. Preserve the execution target and deployed runtime.
